summary: Iter44 end-to-end test: 29/32 backend tests PASS (3 minor issues), 100% frontend smoke PASS on all 4 features. Verified business-address fields, pro-invoices year/month/per_page filtering, /pro-invoices/stats KPIs, /admin/invoices filter+pagination, NEW /api/admin/jobs/{id}, MyInvoicesPage UI (142 invoices, compact action icons, 20/50/100), Admin Billing filter bar, Admin Support drawer JobDetailsPanel + Cancel Job button.

minor.issue: Returns 500 instead of 422 when month is out of range (1-12). Spec requires Query(ge=1, le=12) validation. Root cause: `month` param typed `int` (no bounds) in routes/pro_invoicing_routes.py L187; invalid month then crashes datetime(year, 13, 1) with ValueError. Add `month: Optional[int] = Query(None, ge=1, le=12)`.

Response does not include business_address/business_postal_code/business_city/business_country keys when they were never set in DB (returns raw mongo doc via serialize_doc). After a PATCH writes them, GET returns them. Frontend handles missing keys gracefully (verified), but for API consumers consider normalising defaults in response (return empty string) — minor.

When job has no accepted_quote_id, the `accepted_pro` key is OMITTED from response (instead of returned as null). Spec implies it should always be present (nullable). Also leaks raw mongo `_id` in response. Fix: in admin_routes.py L585 set `js['accepted_pro'] = None` outside the if-block, and `js.pop('_id', None)` before return.

action_items: Add Query(ge=1, le=12) bounds to `month` param in /api/pro-invoices route (currently 500 on month=13).
In GET /api/admin/jobs/{id}: always return `accepted_pro` (null when none) and strip raw mongo `_id` before returning. Optional: same `_id` strip on /api/profile/pro.
Optional: normalise missing business_* keys in /api/profile/pro response so they always exist (empty string).
critical_code_review_comments: pro_invoicing_routes.py uses `int` for query params without bounds — wrap with `Query(..., ge=1, le=12)` for month to avoid 500s.
admin_routes.py GET /jobs/{id} returns serialize_doc(job) which retains `_id` — strip it; also conditional accepted_pro key makes response shape inconsistent.
Multiple endpoints leak mongo `_id` (admin/jobs/{id}, /profile/pro) — consider central serializer that always drops `_id`.
